findings.title: Spec hashes in the manifest don't match the baseline hashes of the HEAD files
findings.message: The manifest pins specs/accessibility.md, specs/rendering.md, specs/platform-support.md and specs/workbench-interaction.md to hashes that differ from the baseline hashes of those files in the review HEAD. If other phases do not rewrite those specs to exactly these bytes, any consumer that checks this manifest against the tree will fail. Alternatively the manifest may have been generated from a different tree than the one being released, so the evidence would not match the shipped sources.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate the manifest from the final integrated tree, after every phase's spec edits have landed, and add a check that recomputes each hash and fails on mismatch.

findings.title: Integrated check relies on cached test results with no provenance
findings.message: Most Go packages in the integrated check report '(cached)', so the log shows Go replaying earlier results rather than running the tests against the snapshot being attested. The snapshot is already marked dirty, and the log carries no commit, archive hash or exit status. That weakens its value as release evidence.
findings.suggestion: Re-run with `go test -count=1 ./...` for the attested snapshot. Record the command, the exit status and the source commit or archive hash in the report, as unit-tests.txt does with its `$` command lines.

findings.title: Private builds silently bundle untracked files
findings.message: In private mode (`include_untracked=not public`), every untracked, non-ignored file under the allowed directories is packaged. These include `scripts`, `examples`, `docs`, `specs` and top-level `.go` files. A stray local credential, scratch file or editor artifact would go into the archive with no warning. The manifest records `clean: false` but does not list the extra files. Only the `.git`-ignored build output is excluded.
findings.suggestion: Require an explicit opt-in flag such as `--include-untracked`, or list the untracked files and fail unless they are confirmed. Add the untracked file names to the manifest.

findings.title: Public archive reads working-tree bytes, not the recorded commit
findings.message: Public archive bytes come from `source.read_bytes()` on working-tree files. The only guarantee that they match the recorded commit is `git status --porcelain`, which is blind to files flagged `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree`. A modified tracked file could therefore be packaged while the manifest claims `clean: true` and names the commit. The archive's provenance would then be false.
findings.suggestion: For public builds, read file contents from the recorded commit (`git ls-tree -r -z HEAD` plus `git cat-file blob`, or `git archive`). Alternatively, fail if `git ls-files -v` reports any flagged files. Also hash the bytes consistently with what is archived.
